turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I am not afraid of threats, Sandip. My concern is for the safety and well-being of my people. Your actions are unacceptable, and you must respect my authority.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Your authority, Nikhil? Is it not I who is the voice of the people, their champion and liberator? You, with your books and your weak-kneed tenants, are a relic of the past.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your rhetoric may sway the masses, Sandip, but it does not change the fact that you are overstepping your bounds. I demand that you cease your interference with my tenants and withdraw from my lands.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Your tenants, my dear Nikhil, are not relics of the past like you. They are the future, the beating heart of our nation, and I am their voice. You cannot silence me or the people I lead.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not stand idly by while you incite my people against me. Your presence here is a violation of my authority, and I demand you respect the boundaries of my lands.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I am torn between you both, Sandip, Nikhil. Your words cut deep, and I fear the consequences of your conflict.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Your fear, my dear Bimala, is misplaced. I am not here to incite, but to awaken. The future belongs to those who seize it, and I shall not retreat from my rightful place in the hearts of the people.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I see the passion in both of your eyes, but fear it may lead to a path neither of you truly wishes to tread.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: The future you speak of is not built on chaos and division, Sandip. I warn you again, cease your disruptive actions or face the consequences.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: And what consequences, pray tell, would you impose, my dear rival? Your authority is as fragile as it is fleeting, Nikhil. The people have seen the light, and I am their beacon.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your arrogance blinds you, Sandip. The people may be swayed by your rhetoric, but they will not tolerate the disruption of their lives. I implore you to reconsider your actions.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Your fear, dear Nikhil, is as misguided as it is amusing. The people see through the fog of your rigid ideals, and they are drawn to the warmth of my flame. I will not be swayed by your warnings.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your stubbornness will be your undoing, Sandip. The consequences I speak of are not idle threats. Mark my words.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Do not fear for me, Nikhil. The storm that brews is but a whisper in the wind compared to the roar of the revolution I have ignited. I shall not be cowed by the shadows of your doubts.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your revolution is built on sand, Sandip. The people may be swayed now, but they will turn against you when they realize the truth of your intentions.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Nikhil, your heart is as heavy with the burdens of the past as it is light with the dreams of the future. But the people, my dear friend, are like the wind; they will follow the direction in which they are guided, and I have shown them the path to a brighter tomorrow.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your arrogance will be your downfall, Sandip. The people may be swayed by your rhetoric now, but the truth will eventually prevail.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: And what truth, pray tell, Nikhil? The truth that the ancients have laid down for us is nothing more than a tired old tapestry, frayed and faded with the wear of centuries. I bring a fresh canvas, and upon it, I paint the future with bold and vibrant strokes.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: The future you paint is one of chaos and division, Sandip. The truth is the stability and order that has sustained our people for generations.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Order and stability, Nikhil? You speak as if they are the pillars of our society, but they are the very chains that bind us to a stagnant past. The future is not a static portrait but a dynamic canvas painted with the colors of change and progress.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ... No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
